text:
Aisha (support): Hey team, customer ACME is reporting huge tail latency from our /v1/generate endpoint since ~09:05 UTC. p99 jumped from ~800ms to ~6s. They provided request IDs and a short repro. They're hitting the hosted API from eu-west-1. :exclamation:
Marco (oncall): I'm looking. Any spikes in inflight requests or queue depth?
Aisha (support): Saved the payload and request ids: rid=acme-337, acme-338, acme-342. They said 429s earlier then long queues.
Priya (eng-sre): Can we get the worker queue length and admission-control logs? Also check if any autoscaler churned.
Luis (infra): Pulling metrics from the serving cluster now. Dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/serving/eu-west-1?range=15m :eyes:
deploy-bot: Deployment 2026.03.15-21 rolled to eu-west-1 at 08:58 UTC by CI. No failures reported.
Marco (oncall): I can already see a bump in queue_length and avg-concurrency per worker. Looks like a batch of high-token requests started at 09:04:30.
Priya (eng-sre): Do we have traces for rid=acme-337? Send the trace id if available.
Aisha (support): Customer included this curl repro they say reproduces the delay:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"'"'long prompt repeated to reach 4k tokens'"'","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Marco (oncall): Thanks. I pulled a trace: trace=trc-9a7f. Root showed long time waiting in admission queue: 4.8s before dispatch to worker. Worker processing time ~600ms. So queueing/backpressure is the culprit, not model runtime.
Priya (eng-sre): Good find. That suggests overloaded workers or misconfigured admission thresholds. Check admission_control.{py,log} for recent changes.
Luis (infra): No recent config changes since yesterday. But the autoscaler didn't add nodes — it hit the maximum reserved for hosted cluster. We're at pool_capacity=120 workers and all at ~95% concurrency.
Aisha (support): Customer is asking for a mitigation now. Can we offer a temporary workaround?
Marco (oncall): Short-term mitigations: 1) Ask customer to reduce concurrency / client-side rate limit, 2) Route their traffic to a lower-concurrency path we can prioritize, or 3) Temporarily bump their request priority if they have enterprise plan. I'll open a ticket with infra to see if we can enable priority routing.
Priya (eng-sre): Also we should return informative 429 with Retry-After when admission queue exceeds threshold. Right now some requests are held silently, causing p99 to grow. We had a knob `admission.max_queue_ms=2000` but looks like it's set to 10000 in eu-west-1 overrides. That explains 4-5s waits.
Marco (oncall): If we lower that to 2000ms, we'll drop overloaded requests faster and surface 429s instead of tails. Pros: reduces p99. Cons: customers see more visible 429s. For ACME we can temporarily reduce to 2s in their region.
Luis (infra): I can patch the config via infra playbook. Running: 
```
infractl patch-config --cluster eu-west-1 --path serving.admission.max_queue_ms --value 2000 --dry-run
```
Marco (oncall): Do dry-run then patch. Also set `serving.admission.prioritize_enterprise=true` for their org id if possible.
Priya (eng-sre): Let's also enable a short-term scaling safety: increase pool_capacity by 20 workers from reserved slack if cloud quota allows. I'll request it.
Aisha (support): I told ACME to reduce concurrency to 2 parallel requests while we act. They've acknowledged.
Luis (infra): Dry-run OK. Applying patch now.
```
infractl patch-config --cluster eu-west-1 --path serving.admission.max_queue_ms --value 2000
Applying patch... OK (request id rq-8872)
```
Marco (oncall): Patch applied. I'm monitoring queue length.
Priya (eng-sre): Also pushed a quick change to admission controller to add a `x-redwood-queue-pos` debug header for internal customers to aid in debugging (will be gated). That landed as a config flip, not full release.
deploy-bot: Config flip `admission-debug-headers` enabled in eu-west-1 by platform-ops.
Marco (oncall): Early signals: p99 fell from ~6s to ~1.1s within 90s, p95 to ~450ms. Queue length dropped.
Aisha (support): Customer reports improvement for now. They still saw some 429s during the window but say overall UX better. :thumbsup:
Priya (eng-sre): Follow-ups: 1) Add a permanent alert for admission queue SRE; current alert only fires on worker CPU. 2) Re-evaluate default admission.max_queue_ms per region; don't allow 10s defaults. 3) Add per-org concurrency caps and priority routing. 4) Update support KB with recommended client-side backoff guidance and example code.
Marco (oncall): I'll create an incident ticket and assign actions. Incident link: https://infra.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-0315-queuebackpressure
Luis (infra): Also opened a cloud quota request to allow +20 workers as standby for peak.
Aisha (support): Logging summary and repro steps I'll paste into the ticket. Repro steps we used:
1) Run the curl above with `-P` parallelism or use artillery to simulate 30 concurrent clients each sending a long prompt.
2) Observe admission queue metric `serving.admission.queue_length` spike and `serving.admission.wait_ms` > 2000ms.
3) After config flip to 2000ms, expect more 429s but lower tail latency.

Example artillery snippet:
```
config:
  target: "https://api.redwood.ai"
  phases:
    - duration: 60
      arrivalRate: 30
scenarios:
  - flow:
    - post:
        url: "/v1/generate"
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer sk_TEST"
        json:
          model: "redwood-large"
          input: "<repeat long prompt>"
          max_tokens: 1024
```

Marco (oncall): Good. Priya, please add a postmortem item to track changing default `max_queue_ms` and adding automatic tenant throttling.
Priya (eng-sre): Will do. I'll also instrument a per-tenant slow-request counter so support can surface impacted customers faster.
Aisha (support): I'll follow up with ACME and keep the ticket open until we're satisfied. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.
Marco (oncall): Closing the operational loop: short-term fix done, monitoring shows improved latency. Will move action items to INC ticket for medium-term changes. :white_check_mark:
